canonical_name: genann -- a minimal feedforward neural network in C (Lewis Van Winkle)
lineage: The perceptron/MLP lineage (Rosenblatt 1958 -> Rumelhart backprop 1986): genann is a tiny ANSI C multilayer perceptron trained by backpropagation -- the connectionist update rule and forward pass in a few hundred readable lines
version: github.com/codeplea/genann master as of 2026-09-12 (commit in hashes)
entry_points: genann_init / genann_train (backprop) / genann_run (forward); the shipped XOR + IRIS examples

example.command: make; run the XOR example -- train a 2-2-1 net by backprop until it learns exclusive-or
example.output: the trained net outputs ~0/1 correctly on all four inputs

upstream_docs: Rumelhart, Hinton, Williams, Learning representations by back-propagating errors, 1986

human_capability_summary.built_to: learn a nonlinear input-output mapping from examples by adjusting connection weights via gradient descent (backpropagation) through a layered network
human_capability_summary.pressure: a mapping (like XOR) that no single linear unit can represent; the network must distribute the function across hidden units and learn the weights from data alone
human_capability_summary.success_means: the trained network generalises the target function (e.g. learns XOR, classifies IRIS) from examples

known_human_problem_solved: supervised learning of nonlinear functions by a connectionist network
human_environmental_pressure: a nonlinearly-separable task, learning from examples only (no programmed rule)
human_failure_condition: failure to converge (bad learning rate / local minimum) or overfitting -- the net memorises noise and does not generalise
behavioral_entry_point: change the learning rate or hidden-layer size, or corrupt the training labels, and watch convergence/generalisation change

nyx_handoff.how_to_run_it: recipe.json (runner docker); python -m techne.fossils.harvest run genann
nyx_handoff.what_humans_used_it_for: learn a nonlinear input-output mapping from examples by adjusting connection weights via gradient descent (backpropagation) through a layered network
